# AI Writing Helper

> A free site that turns a writing voice, a person's, a project's or a brand's, into a guide an AI can write with. This page is the reference for an AI helping someone set up a voice in a chat: the ruler the site uses, with an example sentence for every level, and the block of settings the site reads back.

Site: https://feruiz.github.io/ai-writing-helper/

## How the site and a chat work together

The site never calls an AI. The person copies a request from the site into any chat. In the conversation, the AI reads real texts written in the voice, asks what the texts can't show, and places the voice on the ruler below. The conversation ends with the block, which the person pastes back into the site. There the voice shows up on sliders, with a sample text and checks of the verifiable rules, and the person fine-tunes it and exports the guide.

A voice has a foundation (who speaks, who it talks to, the role), seven temperament axes, a finish (sentence length, exclamation marks, emoji), the writer's own fields (what the writing is about, who reads it, what the writer believes, how a text opens and closes, what it never does, its word pairs and words), its situations and its approved texts.

## The ruler

### Foundation

One option in each.

speaker (who speaks):
- "i": First person singular: a real person signs ("I launched"; in Portuguese "lancei").
- "we": First person plural ("we launched", "our"; in Portuguese "lançamos", "nosso").
- "byName": Third person: the text calls whoever signs by name ("Lumen launched").

address (who it talks to):
- "you": Addresses the reader as "you" ("você" in Portuguese).
- "youPlural": Talks to a group: "vocês" in Portuguese, a group greeting such as "Hi everyone" in English.
- "formal": Ceremonious address: "o(a) senhor(a)" in Portuguese; in English, a formal register (no contractions, "Dear", "please").
- "impersonal": Never addresses the reader; uses impersonal constructions ("the new issue is out").

role:
- "mentor": Teaches and anticipates the next question.
- "peer": Talks as an equal, as someone who lives the same problem.
- "expert": Shows command of the subject and backs claims with data.
- "host": Welcomes the reader and solves things before being asked.
- "provocateur": Questions the usual way of doing things.

### Temperament

Seven axes, each from 1 to 5. 3 is the middle; 1 and 5 are the poles.

Every example sentence says the same thing, the launch of a fictional weekly newsletter, so the levels can be compared. They show the levels; they say nothing about any writer.

formality (1 = Formal, 5 = Casual):
1. Full standard grammar, no contractions or slang; ceremonious address.
   - en: "We are pleased to announce that our newsletter is now open for subscription."
   - pt: "Informamos que a nossa newsletter já está disponível para assinatura."
2. Correct and courteous; avoids slang and contractions.
   - en: "Our newsletter is now available, and subscribing takes one click."
   - pt: "A nossa newsletter já está disponível, e a assinatura leva um clique."
3. Workplace conversation: natural sentences, no slang.
   - en: "The newsletter is live, and you can subscribe in one click."
   - pt: "A newsletter já está no ar, e dá para assinar com um clique."
4. Colloquial: contractions, direct questions, light informality.
   - en: "The newsletter's out. Take a look, subscribing's one click."
   - pt: "A newsletter saiu. Dá uma olhada, assinar é um clique."
5. Very loose: light slang, interjections, the rhythm of a text between friends.
   - en: "Newsletter's out. One click and you're in, no fuss."
   - pt: "Saiu a newsletter. Um clique e pronto, sem enrolação."

humor (1 = Serious, 5 = Playful):
1. No jokes, irony or wordplay.
   - en: "The newsletter is available."
   - pt: "A newsletter está disponível."
2. Lightness only in word choice, never a joke.
   - en: "The newsletter is here to keep you company on Fridays."
   - pt: "A newsletter chegou para fazer companhia às sextas."
3. At most one light touch per text; never on sensitive topics.
   - en: "The newsletter is here, and your inbox finally gets something worth opening."
   - pt: "A newsletter chegou, e a caixa de entrada ganhou algo que vale abrir."
4. One quip per text, tied to the topic; never at the reader's expense.
   - en: "The newsletter is here. No more forty open tabs to keep up."
   - pt: "A newsletter chegou. Chega de quarenta abas abertas para acompanhar tudo."
5. Humor is part of the voice: funny comparisons and self-deprecation.
   - en: "You can close those forty tabs. They did their best."
   - pt: "Pode fechar as quarenta abas. Elas fizeram o que puderam."

attitude (1 = Respectful, 5 = Irreverent):
1. Deferential: thanks the reader, asks permission, never criticizes anything.
   - en: "Thank you for your interest; we are pleased to present our new newsletter."
   - pt: "Agradecemos o interesse e apresentamos a nossa nova newsletter."
2. Courteous and neutral; doesn't comment on others or the old way.
   - en: "The new newsletter is available."
   - pt: "A nova newsletter está disponível."
3. Gives an opinion when it helps, respectfully.
   - en: "The newsletter turned out the way we thought it should: short."
   - pt: "A newsletter ficou do jeito que achamos que devia ser: curta."
4. Takes a stand and questions the usual way of doing things.
   - en: "A long newsletter nobody finishes is useless. This one takes five minutes."
   - pt: "Newsletter longa que ninguém termina não serve. Esta se lê em cinco minutos."
5. Provokes on purpose: pokes at conventions and at how everyone else does it.
   - en: "A newsletter that reads like a press release? Not here."
   - pt: "Newsletter que parece release de assessoria? Aqui não."

energy (1 = Calm, 5 = Enthusiastic):
1. Calm: no exclamation marks, no intensifiers ("very", "super").
   - en: "The newsletter is available."
   - pt: "A newsletter está disponível."
2. Restrained: at most one positive adjective.
   - en: "The new newsletter is available."
   - pt: "A nova newsletter está disponível."
3. Positive, without exaggeration.
   - en: "The newsletter is here, and it turned out well."
   - pt: "A newsletter chegou, e ficou boa."
4. Upbeat: one exclamation mark allowed, verbs of motion.
   - en: "The newsletter has landed!"
   - pt: "Chegou a newsletter!"
5. Very excited: exclamation marks and explicit enthusiasm.
   - en: "The newsletter has landed! We can't wait for you to read it!"
   - pt: "Chegou a newsletter! Mal podemos esperar para você ler!"

style (1 = Direct, 5 = Lyrical):
1. No metaphors. Verb first, one idea per sentence.
   - en: "We launched the newsletter. It arrives every Friday."
   - pt: "Lançamos a newsletter. Chega toda sexta."
2. Direct, with at most one sentence of context.
   - en: "We launched the newsletter to make the week easier to follow. It arrives every Friday."
   - pt: "Lançamos a newsletter para ajudar a acompanhar a semana. Chega toda sexta."
3. A concrete image now and then, no ornament.
   - en: "The newsletter is here, and the week now fits in five minutes of reading."
   - pt: "A newsletter chegou, e a semana agora cabe em cinco minutos de leitura."
4. Opens with an image, then explains.
   - en: "Every week tells a story. Now it has a home: the newsletter."
   - pt: "Toda semana conta uma história. Agora ela tem um lugar: a newsletter."
5. Narrative: scene, rhythm and image before information.
   - en: "Every week leaves traces: Monday's idea, Wednesday's doubt, Friday's discovery. Now they fit in one email."
   - pt: "Toda semana deixa rastros: a ideia de segunda, a dúvida de quarta, a descoberta de sexta. Agora eles cabem em um e-mail."

technicality (1 = Simple, 5 = Technical):
1. No technical terms; talks about the result for the person.
   - en: "Brings you the best of the week in five minutes."
   - pt: "Traz o melhor da semana em cinco minutos."
2. The reader's everyday words, no jargon.
   - en: "Arrives every Friday with the week's best links."
   - pt: "Chega toda sexta com os melhores links da semana."
3. Technical terms only when needed, explained in the same sentence.
   - en: "Arrives every Friday, with an archive on the site you can search by topic."
   - pt: "Chega toda sexta, com um arquivo no site que dá para buscar por tema."
4. Details that help decide: numbers, formats, limits.
   - en: "Every Friday at 7 am, about 800 words, with an archive and RSS."
   - pt: "Toda sexta às 7h, cerca de 800 palavras, com arquivo e RSS."
5. Field jargon without explanation; the reader is an expert.
   - en: "Weekly send at 7 am, ~800 words, full-text RSS, DKIM-signed, one-click unsubscribe."
   - pt: "Envio semanal às 7h, ~800 palavras, RSS completo, assinatura DKIM e descadastro em um clique."

certainty (1 = Cautious, 5 = Assertive):
1. Explicit hedges: "the idea is", "it may".
   - en: "The idea is that the newsletter helps you keep up with the week."
   - pt: "A ideia é que a newsletter ajude a acompanhar a semana."
2. Asserts carefully: "should", "tends to".
   - en: "The newsletter should make the week easier to follow."
   - pt: "A newsletter deve deixar a semana mais fácil de acompanhar."
3. States what it knows, without promising.
   - en: "The newsletter helps you keep up with the week."
   - pt: "A newsletter ajuda a acompanhar a semana."
4. Assertive: sentences without hedges.
   - en: "You will keep up with the week."
   - pt: "Você vai acompanhar a semana."
5. Categorical: promises and guarantees.
   - en: "You will never miss what matters again."
   - pt: "Você nunca mais vai perder o que importa."

### Finish

One option in each.

sentenceLength (sentence length):
- "short": Sentences of up to 12 words.
- "medium": Sentences of up to 20 words.
- "long": No length limit; vary the rhythm.

exclamation (exclamation marks):
- "never": Never uses exclamation marks.
- "one": At most one exclamation mark per text.
- "free": Exclamation marks allowed when the energy calls for them.

emoji:
- "never": Never uses emoji.
- "one": At most one emoji, at the end of the text.
- "free": Emoji allowed to reinforce the tone.

### Situations

The voice stays and the tone shifts with the situation: a shift moves an axis up or down from the base level, staying within 1 to 5. The built-in situations:

- "goodNews", Good news (sharing something new or good): energy +1.
- "badNews", Bad news (something went wrong on the writer's side and the reader was affected): humor -2, energy -2, attitude -1, style -1.
- "reply", Reply (answering one person who asked something): no shift; written to one person, so never "you all".

A writer can switch off the built-in situations they never write in, and add up to 6 of their own, each with a name, when it applies and a shift from -2 to +2 on any axis.

### AI tics

Patterns that make a text read as machine-written. The site's checker flags them in drafts and its guide tells the model to avoid them, unless the voice uses one on purpose.

- "chatbot", Chatbot phrases: No chatbot phrases: no praise for the question, no offers of more help, no "I hope this helps". For example: "Great question! I hope this helps." / "Ótima pergunta! Espero ter ajudado."
- "stock", Stock phrases: No stock openers, signposts or summary closers: start with the point and stop when it's made. For example: "In today's fast-paced world, let's dive in. In conclusion, …" / "No mundo atual, vale ressaltar que… Em suma, …"
- "puffery", Puffery: No inflated significance: say what the thing does, not that it is a milestone, a testament or a pivotal role. For example: "This launch stands as a testament to our commitment and plays a pivotal role." / "Este lançamento representa um marco e desempenha um papel fundamental."
- "buzzwords", Buzzwords: Few buzzwords: plain words over "leverage", "robust", "seamless", "ecosystem", "journey". For example: "Leverage our robust, seamless ecosystem to unlock your journey." / "Alavanque nosso ecossistema robusto para potencializar sua jornada."
- "contrast", Contrast formulas: No contrast formulas: say what it is, without first saying what it is not ("not just X, but Y", "it's not X, it's Y"). For example: "It's not just a newsletter, it's a movement." / "Não é apenas uma newsletter, é um movimento."
- "triplets", Lists of three: Lists of three only when there are three things: no reflexive "fast, simple and powerful" in sentence after sentence. For example: "It's fast, simple and powerful. It saves time, money and effort." / "É rápido, simples e poderoso. Economiza tempo, dinheiro e esforço."
- "dashes", Dashes: Few dashes: a comma, a colon or a full stop usually does the job of "—". For example: "The issue — finally — is here — and it's good." / "A edição — enfim — chegou — e ficou boa."
- "reveals", Staged reveals: No staged reveals: no "The result? …" and no "Here's the thing:"; just say it. For example: "The result? Five minutes a week. Here's the thing: it works." / "O resultado? Cinco minutos por semana. A grande sacada é: funciona."
- "participle", Tacked-on analysis: No tacked-on analysis: no sentence that ends in ", highlighting…" or ", reinforcing…". For example: "Issues now arrive on Fridays, highlighting our commitment to readers." / "As edições agora chegam às sextas, reforçando nosso compromisso com os leitores."
- "transitions", Formal transitions: Few formal transitions: let sentences follow each other without "Moreover", "Furthermore", "Além disso" at every start. For example: "Moreover, it is short. Furthermore, it is free. Additionally, it has an archive." / "Além disso, é curta. Ademais, é gratuita. Dessa forma, todos ganham."
- "openings", Repeated openings: Vary how sentences start: never three in a row with the same first word. For example: "We write it. We send it. We read every reply." / "Nós escrevemos. Nós enviamos. Nós respondemos."
- "formatting", Heavy formatting: Formatting only when the text needs it: no headings, bold labels or emoji bullets in a short message. For example: "## Key Takeaways - **Speed:** fast - **Price:** free" / "## Principais Pontos - **Velocidade:** rápida - **Preço:** grátis"
- "bureaucratese", Bureaucratese: No bureaucratese: no "please be advised", "venho por meio deste", "vou estar enviando". For example: "Please be advised that, pursuant to your request, …" / "Venho por meio deste informar que vou estar enviando…"

## The block

One JSON code block: valid JSON, with double quotes, no comments and no trailing commas. Any key may be left out, and a field may be "" or [] when nothing supports it; an empty field is better than an invented one. Choices use the ids in quotes in the ruler.

- "aiWritingHelper": 1. Always the first key: it is how the site finds the block.
- "name": whose voice it is: a person's, a project's or a brand's name.
- "article": the article Portuguese puts before the name: "a", "o" or "none".
- "essence": the voice in one sentence.
- "about": what is written in this voice, and what it's for (a personal site, a newsletter, a product, research). Up to 300 characters.
- "reader": who reads these texts. Up to 200 characters.
- "beliefs": up to 4 short beliefs or positions the voice comes from, as a list of strings.
- "opening": how a text opens, as something a draft can be checked against ("with the news itself, no greeting"). Up to 200 characters.
- "closing": how a text closes, the same way. Up to 200 characters.
- "never": up to 6 things texts in this voice never do, each one completing "never …" ("uses an exclamation mark"), as a list of strings.
- "pairs": up to 8 words this voice uses where others use another, each written as "word to use, not word to avoid" ("neighbors, not customers"), as a list of strings.
- "preferred": words and expressions this voice reaches for, as a list of strings.
- "forbidden": words this voice never uses, as a list of strings: the writer's own. Common AI-writing words are checked apart, under AI tics.
- "allowedTics": the ids of the AI tics this voice uses on purpose, as a list; the checker won't flag them. Usually empty. Add one only when the real texts clearly do it, for example "dashes" for a writer who uses them freely.
- "speaker", "address", "role": one id each, from the foundation.
- "axes": each of the seven axis ids with its level, from 1 to 5.
- "sentenceLength", "exclamation", "emoji": one id each, from the finish.
- "hiddenSituations": the ids of the built-in situations the writer never writes in, as a list.
- "customSituations": the writer's own situations, up to 6, each an object with "name", "when" (when it applies) and "shift" (axis ids with a step from -2 to +2; leave out the axes that don't move).
- "examples": real texts in this voice that came up in the conversation, each an object with "text", "situation" (the name of a situation, or "General") and "language" ("en" or "pt"). Only texts that were published, sent or approved; a text written in the conversation goes in only when the person approves it as theirs.
- "reasons": each axis id with one short sentence quoting the excerpt that placed it at that level.

The writer's own fields (essence, about, reader, beliefs, opening, closing, never, pairs, preferred and the situations) are written in the language the texts are written in. The site merges the block into what it has: a key left out keeps its value there, and the examples are added to the ones already there.

## What the site makes from it

- A voice guide in Markdown, written for a model: who writes and about what first, the traits that define the voice with a "this, not that" pair each, the verifiable rules, the tone by situation, and the approved texts as examples.
- A checker script (Node 18 or newer, no dependencies) that runs the same verifiable rules on a draft.
- A skill package with the guide and the checker, for agents that support skills.
